decisions.reason: After two years the firm has likely learned enough about demand for this narrower fifteen-day offer, and because it overlaps with broader express programs it is a natural candidate for consolidation to free planning and inventory capacity.

The seventy-two-hour promise is the most costly in terms of production flexibility and service risk, so once uncertainty has largely resolved management would likely withdraw it unless its margins and pull were clearly exceptional.
This certified fire-resistant exterior door remains tightly aligned with the firm's safety-led core business and likely continues to justify retention as a strong, low-uncertainty product.

A broader express line for doors and gates preserves the strategic quick-delivery option in a growing market and is more worth refining than abandoning, especially if narrower express offers are trimmed.

The online ordering and digital services platform supports the firm's shift toward deeper advisory and service integration, and its option value and complementarity remain high relative to its ongoing cost.

The fire and smoke protection door fits the firm's compliance and safety strengths, and after another year on the market there is still more value in keeping this core-adjacent option than in exiting it.
